review: 1:3–1:4 תַּחַת־דֶּגֶל אַהֲבָתוֹ — Song of Songs 2:4 (וְדִגְלוֹ עָלַי אַהֲבָה); the Arabic وَتَحْتَ لِوَا حُبِّهِ is that banner, and דֶּגֶל is the word of the verse.

3:3 וְהַמָּן וְהַצּוּר — Exodus 16:15 (מָן) with 1 Cor 10:4 (וְהַצּוּר הָיָה הַמָּשִׁיחַ); the Arabic وَالْمَنُّ وَالصَّخْرُ is that pair, and the Hebrew keeps the wilderness nouns rather than a general 'food'.

3:1–3:2 לַחְמֵנוּ הַנֶּחְמָד / בְּכֹל יְמֵי הַמַּסָּע — the Arabic طَعَامُنَا الشَّهِيّ / فِي مُدَّةِ السَّيْر is 'our delicious food during the journey'; נֶחְמָד is the niphal participle of חמד ('desirable'), the adjective of Gen 3:6 and Isa 53:2.

4:2 סְעוּ הָלְאָה — the Arabic سِيرُوا إِلَى الْأَمَام is 'march forward'; הָלְאָה ('onward, further') is biblical (Gen 19:9), so the line keeps the imperative without resorting to the Modern Hebrew קָדִימָה.
